comment: The draft explains the progression from data models to actors, FHIR profiles and testing, but it does not require explicit end-to-end traceability from an approved professional or clinical semantic requirement into the implemented model, terminology binding, storage, exchange, analytics/AI use and conformance test. Without traceability, an implementation can be syntactically conformant while progressively losing the rationale and meaning that the original content governance approved.

public.text: The draft explains the progression from data models to actors, FHIR profiles and testing, but it does not require explicit end-to-end traceability from an approved professional or clinical semantic requirement into the implemented model, terminology binding, storage, exchange, analytics/AI use and conformance test. Without traceability, an implementation can be syntactically conformant while progressively losing the rationale and meaning that the original content governance approved.
public.suggestedRevision: Require a traceability chain for priority clinical content: governed requirement to logical information model, to terminology/value-set binding and to implementation profile, to persistence/provenance requirements and to exchange transaction, to analytics/AI use and to conformance and regression tests. Material deviations and local extensions should be documented with rationale and clinical approval.
